## The runs, as changed
1. **Order.** The rule's "base, the change, base again, 5 rounds alternated" becomes 12 rounds in a Williams order of
the three builds:
- A is the base, B is D1, and C is the base again, the same file as A.
- The rows are ABC, BCA, CAB, CBA, ACB and BAC, run twice; round r runs row r mod 6. In each six rounds, each
build takes each position twice and follows each other build twice.
- Why 12 and not 6: see the first null session, below.
- Why: in step 1 the first run of a round was the slow one (amendment 1). The stamped alternation keeps the change
in the middle and the bases at the ends, so a build's time cannot be told from its position.
- A known limit: B follows a run of the other file in 4 of the 6 rows (A and C in 2 each). Each run is a fresh
process timed after its own warm-up, with the same kernels, so this is taken as negligible; the null sessions
cannot see it, since their three builds are one file.
2. **A head run.** Before each case in each round, the row's first build runs once and is set aside, as in
amendment 1.
3. **The unmasked round** becomes an unmasked session of 12 rounds on the same rows, at water 12,288 and 98,304 atoms in
float32 with tables, run right after the P-cores session. One round cannot balance the positions, and the rule's
lesson 3 speaks of "the unmasked rounds".
4. **Held to the P-cores.** The P-cores session's runner checks that its process holds the mask 0xFFFC
(`tools/pk/affine.py`); the unmasked session's runner checks that it holds every processor of the system. Each run
inherits the runner's mask.
5. **The card**, by `tools/ht/gpu_busy.ps1`.
- Busy means a program other than ours above 30% of a 3D engine. The check leaves out by name omnimd, Python,
Docker's virtual machine (vmmem, vmwp), dp, lmp and cargo's test binaries, and the desktop's own (wallpaper,
dwm, explorer). GPU work of those kinds is kept off only by the rule beside the sessions (below). A check whose
counter gives no samples reads free.
- It is checked before a round, and the round waits while another program uses it.
- It is checked again before each case and at the end of the round. If any of these checks finds it busy, the
round is voided: its runs stay in the record, set aside, and its row runs again once the card is free.
- A session stops without a decision if it voids more than 6 rounds, waits more than 2 hours for the card in
all, or has a check that exits with an error or does not exit within 120 s.
6. **A failed run stops the session.** A failed run is one that exits with an error, prints output the runner cannot
read or lacks a line it reads, falls back from the tables, or takes more than 1,800 s. Any other error of the
runner stops it too. The record is written before the runner exits, with every run made so far and the reason
(the build, the case, and the last lines of stderr without the lines that hold times).
- A stop caused by a run of B means D1 is not kept and the session is not rerun, unless the cause is shown to lie
outside the build (the card, the runner, the machine); such a stop is handled as any other stop below.
- The runner labels every exception of a run "could not read its output", and the exception named in the reason
decides where the cause lies. An OSError raised when the build's process is started (it never ran) is judged
under "unless the cause is shown to lie outside the build". An exception raised while reading what the build
printed (a JSON, key or index error) is the build's unreadable output.
- An error exit of B counts as a failure of clause 3:
the hazard of amendment 5 item 4 shows as one, since the check pass ends in a validation that refuses a value
missing or not finite, and a pass that did not write in place is an error. A timeout or a fallback of B fails
D1 but is not itself a result of clause 3.
- The held problems of every run in a stopped record count for clause 3 as well, read from the record by hand,
since the reading refuses a stopped record.
- Any other stop is without a decision. Such a session is rerun from the start into a new file once the cause is
known, and only for a cause outside the build (`step2-notes.md`, lines 70-71). The stopped record is kept, and
its times are not read until the rerun is decided.
- If the cause is in the runner, its fix is set by an amendment of its own before the rerun.

## The reading
- **The measure of a case** is the least, over the 12 rounds done, of the timed loop's `ms_per_eval`, head runs and
voided rounds set aside: the rule's "the least of each case is kept". Each line of `--bench-batches` is a case of
its own.
- ratio = least B / least A - 1.
- **The spread** is the rank spread: the 14th fastest of the case's 24 base runs (A's and C's together) over least A,
less 1. The rule names the spread but does not define it.
- So ratio > spread exactly when B's least lies above that run, that is when the 14 fastest of the case's 36 runs
are all the base's.
- For a build no different from the base, that has chance C(24,14)/C(36,14) = 0.052% at a case if its 36 runs are
exchangeable, at most 1.4% at any of the 27 cases. If they are exchangeable only within each round, the worst
case is the 14 fastest spread over the 12 rounds, two in each of two: (1/3)^2 (2/3)^10 = 0.19% at a case, at
most 5.2% at any of 27. Neither figure is fitted to data.
- Exchangeable within a round means no effect of position: the rows balance one but do not randomize it. In the
first null the P-cores session shows none (150 case-rounds; mean rank within the round by position 2.06, 1.95
and 1.99; fastest 46, 50 and 54 times). The unmasked session is too small to tell (12 case-rounds), though it
leans to position 2 (mean ranks 2.50, 1.42 and 2.08; fastest 1, 8 and 3 times). The second null's records can
be read the same way; its rank test alone cannot show such an effect.
- Why the 14th: the first null's rounds differ (its rounds 4 and 6 ran slower), so the within-round figure is the
one taken. 14 is the run whose within-round worst case over the 27 cases is near 5%: the 13th gives 10.4% and
the 15th 2.6%, at a cost in power. At the 6-round analogue (the 7th fastest of a case's 12 base runs over least
A, less 1) the first null passes (hap0 +1.37% against 1.58%). It would pass from the 6th of 12 (1.39%) and fail
at the 5th (1.29%), so the run was not set at the least that passes it.
- The one-draw spread, |least C / least A - 1| as `tools/fit/decide_ab.py` read it for PR C, is printed beside it
and decides nothing. The first null session shows why (below): with it, the base alone trips clause 1 in about
44% of sessions of 6 rounds and 26% of 12 (`run/prd-d1-null/bootstrap-1.txt`).
- What the rank spread costs: at a case whose base runs scatter widely, the bound widens to that scatter, so a
small real slowdown there goes unseen. In the first null the 6-round analogue was above 1% at 7 of the 27
and s-w192 x4 1.87% (from `null-pcores-1.json`). So at hap0 and w1536, on D1's path, a slowdown of about 1.5%
and 1.2% could go unseen, and on some batch lines one of 2% to 3%. At 12 rounds, by draws with replacement from
each case's 18 runs (rough, as in `bootstrap-1.txt`; round effects ignored), the bound's median is about 1.4% at
hap0, 1.15% at w1536 and 1.7% at s-w1536, and up to 2.4% on the batch lines (s-ser88 x4, 3.6% at its 90th
percentile), above 1% at 10 of the 27 cases. This is accepted for D1: at these cases the base alone differs by
that much between runs.
- At w98304 the base is tight: in the first null's P-cores session its 18 runs lay within 0.89% of each other
(1.34% unmasked), and the analogue was 0.25% in the P-cores session and 0.45% unmasked (from
`null-pcores-1.json` and `null-unmasked-1.json`). So the bound of clauses 1 and 2 there was expected to stay at
the 1% floor. The second null did not bear this out: its sessions drifted, and the bound at w98304 read 1.15% in
the P-cores session and 1.61% unmasked (see its result, below).
- The chances above are of a false slower only. Clause 2's event, ratio below -max(spread, 1%), is not a rank
